session:
PTY multiplexer (replaces tmux). Create terminals, send input (send-keys), read output (capture-pane), manage lifecycle.

Actions:
- list: Optional session_id scopes one session; full rows expose known last_activity_ms. compact=true derives activity_age_ms from it (null when unknown) and keeps identity, state and omitted_fields. All active sessions and states in one call, including local and connected remote sessions. Remote rows carry connection_id and address=connection/session_id. Use for every global overview; never fan out per-session status calls. Returns display_name (assigned name), alias (independent repo-derived short address), tuic_session (the stable identity the tab persists), is_caller, shell_state (PTY activity), and agent_state (starting|working|awaiting_input|idle|completed; completed requires suggest marker). Absent optional fields are omitted, not null — background_work and standby appear only when true.

Every action that takes session_id accepts the PTY id, tuic_session, alias (e.g. tu-1), a unique short PTY-id prefix, or a unique display name.
- create: New PTY. Returns {session_id}. Optional: cwd, shell, rows, cols.
- submit: Submit one non-empty command to a confirmed-idle managed agent and wait internally for a bounded receipt. Use one call; never split text and Enter; never poll after it. Returns submission_id, submitted, write_state, acknowledged, retry_safe, turn_epoch, composer_state (tracked InputLineBuffer, not application state), and acknowledgement or a precise reason. Acknowledgement means child terminal movement after Enter, not semantic application acceptance. Never queues; partial composers, dialogs, busy agents, and older queued commands reject before writing.
- force_retry: Submit /retry once to an ego terminal currently reporting provider recovery. Requires session_id; never queues or retries automatically.
- input: Raw text/key compatibility surface. Send text and/or special_key; ok confirms PTY write only.
- output: Read terminal output. Optional byte_budget=1024..65536 returns JSON-text chunks bounded by compact response-envelope UTF-8 bytes (not MCP framing); concatenate chunk values then parse JSON. Follow the opaque continuation with the same action/session; expires after 300s or cache eviction. Omit byte_budget to keep the existing shape. Returns {data, cursor, scrollback_lines, oldest_offset, exited, exit_code}. Use as an anomaly fallback for a child that failed to send its result, not as the normal orchestration channel. The tail read omits an empty input box and everything below it (status line, HUD); format=raw keeps them. scrollback_lines = total lines in buffer (up to 10000); oldest_offset = first available line number. Patterns: (1) Snapshot: omit since_cursor, default limit=50 gives last 50 lines. (2) Delta read: since_cursor=<previous cursor> returns only new lines. (3) Navigate backwards: from_line=oldest_offset reads from the beginning of the buffer. (4) Arbitrary window: from_line=N, limit=50 reads any 50-line slice. Windowed reads report has_more and next_cursor; follow the continuation note to fetch retained output without rerunning the command. Raw pages use from_byte=oldest_offset then from_byte=next_cursor (source-byte positions). Evicted output cannot be recovered.
- declare_worktree: Declare an existing linked worktree for this authenticated live caller. Requires worktree_path; rejects foreign sessions and repositories. Persists sidebar placement without changing shell cwd. Caller-bound MCP-only request, available via POST /mcp.
- status: Session state; absent optional fields are omitted.
- wait: Block (server-side) until session_id is idle or exited (until=idle|exited), or timeout_ms elapses. One cheap call instead of a status polling loop. Returns {met, timed_out, shell_state?, exit_code?}.
- resize: Change PTY dimensions.
- rename: Set the tab's display name. Requires name (non-empty). Sticky by default — protected from later OSC/intent title updates unless is_custom=false.
- keep_open: Keep a managed child open by disabling idle closure with enabled=true; enabled=false restores automatic idle closure. Requires session_id.
- suspend: End the tab's PTY and agent to free memory and CPU but keep the tab, restorable like after a TUIC restart; the user resumes it from the tab. Refused while the agent is working, a question awaits an answer, or a command runs. Not auto-standby, which only SIGSTOPs and keeps memory. Requires session_id.
- close: Graceful shutdown (Ctrl+C, waits).
- kill: Force SIGKILL (use when close fails).
- pause: Pause output buffering. resume: Resume.
agent:
AI agent orchestration. There is no separate swarm action: use these agent/session primitives to spawn and coordinate managed peers.

Orchestration in 5 lines:
1. Managed PTYs auto-bind from $TUIC_SESSION. A headerless external caller calls register without tuic_session to receive an MCP-scoped UUID, or supplies an explicit stable UUID to reclaim it.
2. Spawn a named peer: spawn name=worker prompt=<task> [agent_type=codex|gemini|...] → {session_id, name}.
3. Wait for it: agent action=wait (new mail; omit since, the cursor is kept server-side) or session action=wait session_id=<id> until=idle|exited. Cheap blocking call — do NOT poll in a loop. Both cap at 300s: for work that runs longer, or across a reconnect, poll the spawn's task_id with agent action=task_get instead — the outcome is recorded even with nobody waiting.
4. Talk to it: send to=<peer> message=<text> [urgency=normal|urgent|interrupt]. Normal is the default; use urgent when the recipient must change course before its next step. For normal and urgent mail, the payload is never typed into the recipient's composer. It waits in the recipient's inbox, and an idle/completed recipient may be sent a payload-free generic `agent action=inbox` wake. Urgent sends a payload-free inbox notice to a safe busy Claude/Codex/ego composer for the next tool boundary.
5. Lifecycle notifications carry state only. Every worker must report task output or blockers with send; use session output only if a child anomalously failed to send.

Actions:
- launch: One durable idempotent managed launch (localhost only). Requires idempotency_key, parent_session_id (registered peer), stable name, keep_open, workspace={existing_path} or {repo_path,branch,base_ref?}, and spawn={prompt,...spawn options}. Read a receipt with launch_id alone, or retry the identical request after a lost reply: the same launch_id/session_id returns, never another checkout or PTY. Conflicting key reuse errors explicitly. Receipt status=created|prompt_delivered|ready|blocked, prompt_delivery=queued|delivered|unknown and warm_artifacts are separate. Delivered proves argv handoff or PTY submission, not model acceptance; ready also requires native Ready-screen evidence. Interrupted uncertain creation blocks rather than spawning again; retain the handle and inspect the named resources. Model/account/brief policy remains caller-owned. Also POST /agents/launch and managed_agent_launch IPC, with identical validation.
- spawn: Launch agent in new PTY (localhost only). Optional name is assigned before prompt delivery. Returns {session_id, name, task_id, poll_interval_ms, server_ts, parent_session_id?}.
- task_get: Read a task_id owned by the spawning caller. Returns {task_id, status, status_message?, result?, error_detail?, poll_interval_ms}; optional fields are omitted. Status is working|input_required|completed|failed|cancelled; the last three are immutable. Poll no faster than poll_interval_ms. Outcomes survive client reconnects for up to 24h within this server process.
- task_cancel: Mark an owned task_id cancelled (localhost only). Does NOT kill the PTY; use session action=kill for that. Already-final tasks return their unchanged status with cancelled=false.
- wait: Block until new inbox mail. Not byte-bounded: byte_budget/continuation are rejected before mail consumption; use inbox for bounded payloads. Omit `since` — the server resumes from your last read position; pass it only to override (since=0 replays everything). Success inlines every retained fresh message (up to the 100-message inbox capacity) in chronological order. Every response carries next_since, timeout included. An active wait suppresses terminal wake.
- register: Bind an external/headerless caller, or rename/set the repository path of an auto-bound managed peer. tuic_session is optional; omission generates a stable identity for this MCP connection. Reconnecting under a NEW uuid? Pass `replaces=<old_uuid>` or its inbox is stranded — the response reports superseded_identity, mail_migrated, and mail_stranded + identity_warning when the old identity still owns a live PTY (its mail is left alone). Check `terminal` in the response: false means no PTY notice can be typed into you; a subscribed ACP inbox can still notify you or wake idle ego. Otherwise consume mail with wait/inbox. Declare the orchestrator role with orchestrator=true and remove it with false; spawning a child never infers it, and omitting the field preserves the current role. The response reports mail_wake=managed_pty_lifecycle when a wake can reach you; external/headerless peers without a subscribed ACP inbox stay wait/inbox-only.
- list_peers: Optional to scopes a recipient through the same resolver as send; compact=true returns identity, state (unknown if absent), activity_age_ms (null if absent), and omitted_fields. List peers across the desktop mail hub and connected daemons. address is connection/peer_id (local/peer_id on the hub); connection_id selects one daemon. Returns tuic_session, name, orchestrator, plus alias and session_id for a peer that owns a live terminal. Optional: path filter. Absent fields are omitted.
- send: Message any local or remote peer (requires to, message). Use to=connection/peer_id or connection_id with a daemon-local address. The owning daemon performs inbox delivery and wake; replies return through the desktop hub. `to` accepts the peer's tuic_session, PTY id, or terminal alias. `urgency` is normal (default) or urgent; use urgent when the recipient must change course before its next step. Urgent keeps the body in the inbox and writes only a notice to a safe busy Claude/Codex/ego composer. `urgent_delivered` reports a PTY notice, subscribed ACP inbox update, inbox read, or waiter; false adds `urgent_fallback_reason` for queued mail. It does not prove model action or interrupt a tool. `delivered` and `delivery_path` describe the routing path; `recipient_state` appears only for a managed PTY. Opt-in urgency=interrupt sends Esc to a safe working Claude Code, Codex or ego, waits up to 10 seconds for confirmed idle, then submits the full message as one new input (including for an orchestrator). An already idle recipient needs no Esc. A dialog/approval or draft blocks both Esc and payload. Unsupported agents, no PTY and idle timeout use the existing urgent notice/inbox fallback. The result adds interrupt_delivered and interrupt_fallback_reason; delivery_path=interrupt_payload_and_inbox means the full input was written, not that the model acted. Interrupted tools can leave partial work; child processes may continue. An active waiter owns delivery and needs no interrupt.
- inbox: Optional byte_budget=1024..65536 returns JSON-text chunks; the budget includes the compact page envelope, not MCP framing. Concatenate chunk values then parse JSON; continue with the opaque continuation and same action. Snapshots expire after 300s or cache eviction; errors require a fresh read. The server cursor advances only on the final chunk. Read up to 100 retained messages in FIFO order. Returns next_since and has_more; repeat while has_more is true. Optional: limit (default 100, max 100), since (omit to resume from the server-side cursor). On FIFO eviction, missed_count reports unread messages lost since the last inbox read.
- subscribe: Create or resume a durable independent reader with subscription_id (1..64 ASCII letters/digits/_/-) and filter=actionable (default), all, exit or failure. Actionable excludes routine system lifecycle/idle traffic, not peer mail. A subscription does not consume legacy inbox or another reader.
- inbox/wait with subscription_id: Return up to limit (1..100) matching journal messages, cursor, acknowledged_cursor, missed_count and has_more. No byte_budget/continuation; ACK then read has_more batches. Reads do not acknowledge. An unacknowledged batch is replayed unchanged while retained. wait returns only for matching mail or matching retention loss; routine traffic stays inside the server. For continuous event-driven delivery use GET /agent/subscriptions/{id}/events with your Mcp-Session-Id header, or over ACP subscribe to resource tuic://inbox/subscriptions/{id}.
- ack: Acknowledge a processed subscription batch with subscription_id and its cursor. Acknowledged results never replay on reconnect under the same peer identity and subscription_id. Lost replies before ack can replay: deduplicate side effects by message id. Journal retains the newest 1000 messages per peer across restarts; missed_count counts matching unacknowledged evictions, not routine filtered events. since is legacy-only.
- unsubscribe: Delete one subscription cursor; retained mail and other readers are unchanged.
repo:
Repository and version control. Query workspace repos, their GitHub PR/CI status, and manage git worktrees.

Actions:
- add: Register and activate an existing local directory. Requires absolute path. Persists a usable Git or shell workspace, preserves existing terminals/settings on repeat calls, and broadcasts repositories-changed. No desktop URL handler required; does not spawn a terminal. Returns ok, path, name, branch, is_git_repo, and an optional watcher warning.
- list: Open repos with branch, dirty status, worktrees.
- active: Focused repo path, branch, group.
- status: Cross-repo GitHub PR and CI summary {path, branch, ahead, behind, open_prs, failing_ci}. Optional path limits it to that registered repo; an unregistered path is an error.
- branch_integrations: Integration status and proof for every local branch, including worktree_paths. Requires path.
- branch_integration: Same verdict for one branch. Requires path and branch. Returns tip, integrated, proof, archive_required, archived and archive_ref. Content-based proof requires an archive at that tip before deletion; unknown is never proof.
- worktree_list: Worktrees for a repo. Requires path. Each entry includes lifecycle_status {commit_status: merged|unmerged|in_sync|unknown, dirty_files, removal_safety: safe|requires_force|unknown}, the same verdict worktree_lifecycle and the sidebar use.
- worktree_lifecycle: Fresh safety, fingerprint and submodule commit counts. Requires path and branch.
- worktree_create: Create a linked worktree. Requires path. Optional: branch, base_ref, spawn_session (starts a bare shell PTY, not an agent). Refs and objects are shared with the parent; parent tracked changes are not copied. Git-ignored build directories warm in the background. Wait for warm_artifacts.status in worktree_list to become done or failed before installing dependencies or building.
- worktree_remove: Remove worktree. Requires path and branch, or path and worktree_path for a detached checkout (removed only when clean, reachable from a branch and free of live sessions).
- orphan_cleanup_answer: Answer the pending orphan-removal dialog for path with decision=remove|keep; remove rechecks every worktree for uncommitted/untracked files and branch reachability.
- branch_delete: Delete only a local branch with no checkout after proving its commits are integrated or preserved. Requires path and branch. Proof is in_sync, a merge proof, patch_equivalence, or archived (refs/archive/<branch> points at the exact tip; the response then carries archive_ref and the archive ref is kept). Refuses current/default branches, unmerged commits with no exact archive, and unsafe or changed refs; never touches a remote.
- work_item: Read Tasks detail and comments. Omit the target for the caller worktree link, or pass reference {providerId,accountId,id}, url, or key with provider_id/account_id. Pass cursor from comments.nextCursor for another comment page (limit 1..100, default 50). All provider text is returned in an untrusted-content block. Requires a running frontend with the provider loaded.
- work_item_act: Comment or transition through the Tasks provider. Requires mcp_work_item_writes=true (default false) and operation {kind:comment|transition,value:string}; transition values are provider action IDs, not labels. Uses the same target selection. A timed-out write may have completed: read before retrying.
- progress_list: The project's journal, newest first, paged with total and nextCursor. Requires path. Optional input.blockedOnly, input.ptyId, input.limit (default 8, maximum 100), input.cursor (previous nextCursor). Record a NEW outcome with the `progress` tool, not here.
ui:
Control TUIC UI. Actions:
- tab: open/update panel tab. Requires id, title, + html OR url.
- toast: non-blocking notification. Requires title. Optional: message, level (info/warn/error), sound, urgency (normal/urgent).
- confirm: blocking dialog, shown on every client (desktop, browser, mobile PWA) plus a mobile push — the first answer wins. Returns {confirmed}, plus {reason} when it expired unanswered after 300s (treat that as a refusal, not a yes). Requires title, except settings proposals: pass proposalId to show the backend redacted diff; model title/message/confirmed cannot grant approval.
- design_start: start Design Mode with session_id and optional browser/url. Requires a live terminal agent.
- design_stop: stop the caller-bound repository (repo_path).
- design_status: list Design Mode bindings for an armed caller.
- design_reload: reload the reviewed tab (repo_path).
- design_navigate: navigate the reviewed tab (repo_path, url); remote hosts require an extension host grant.
- design_screenshot: capture the reviewed tab as a PNG path (repo_path).
- design_errors: read captured page errors (repo_path).
- design_eval: evaluate script in the reviewed tab (repo_path, script); requires an explicit optional extension host grant.
- screenshot: capture a panel as WebP. Requires id. Returns {path}. Read the path to view.

URL schemes for tab:
- http(s): loaded in sandboxed iframe using the permissive default-src CSP (external HTTPS and localhost HTTP supported). Site frame policies can still refuse embedding.
- file:///path: read via IPC and rendered as inline HTML (sandbox blocks direct file:// access).
- tuic://edit/<path>?line=N: native code editor (no iframe). Prefix absolute paths with `//` (tuic://edit//Users/x/a.rs). Relative = active repo.
- tuic://open/<path>: native markdown/preview tab.

- tuic://open-repo is rejected; use repo action=add with path to register a directory. Other tuic actions are not tab content.

Custom schemes (vscode://) do NOT work in iframes.

Use:
- A project outcome — a milestone, a decision, a discovery, a blocker — belongs to the `progress` tool, which records it AND shows a toast. `ui action=toast` is the transient half only: it says something happened and keeps no record of it.
- toast for done/error/long-job end; error=failure, warn=recoverable. Skip for micro-steps.
- toast urgency: normal (default) records the notice in the bell only; urgent also shows a transient card on the desktop window. The caller chooses; the card never covers the focused input.
- toast with sound=attention when you are working unattended and are BLOCKED on the user (question, approval, ambiguous requirement). It is the only sound that carries across a room; do not spend it on progress updates.
- confirm BEFORE destructive ops (rm -rf, git reset --hard, force-push, DROP). Only proceed if confirmed.
- tab http(s) for dashboards, reports, >20-line structured output.
- tab tuic://edit to point user at source file+line (review, bug discussion) — beats pasting snippets.
- screenshot to visually verify rendered HTML content in a panel you created.
voice:
Speak a reply out loud, when the user is talking to you hands-free.

Only works while the user has armed hands-free dictation for YOUR terminal: speech belongs to that conversation, not to the application. Call action=status first — if available is false, the reason says why and you must reply in text as usual. Nothing here replaces your normal reply; speaking is in addition to it.

The conversation announces itself. Arming sends you a line saying hands-free voice is now on for this terminal; ending it sends one saying it is off. Both come from TUICommander rather than from the user, and the second is final — after it this tool reports available false and you reply in text again. The user can turn those notices off, so their absence is not proof either way: action=status is.

You do not choose the language or the voice. Both belong to the conversation: the voice is the one for the language the user is speaking, reported as status.language, and it will happily pronounce text in any other language badly. Write the reply in status.language — the same language the hands-free entry told you to answer in.

Accepting a reply is NOT the same as the user hearing it. action=speak returns an utterance_id in state 'queued'; rendering takes seconds and the user can talk over it at any moment. Poll action=status with that utterance_id to learn the outcome: 'finished' means it was heard to the end, 'interrupted' means the user started talking (normal, not an error), 'failed' means it was never audible.

Actions:
- speak: Queue one spoken reply. Requires text (max 2000 characters). Optional turn: the turn you are answering, from an earlier status or from the hands-free notice. Supply it — a reply written for a turn the user has already talked over is then refused instead of spoken over whatever they said next. Omitting it means 'right now'. Returns {utterance_id, state, turn}.
- stop: Stop talking immediately and drop anything queued. Opens a new turn. Use it when you realise the reply in progress is wrong.
- status: {available, unavailable_reason, session_id, language, turn, voice, queued, rendering, speaking, last_error}. Optional utterance_id adds {utterance: {utterance_id, state, error?}} for that one reply; a reply too old to remember comes back as state 'unknown'.
automations: One-shot: {"action":"create","definition":{"name":"Recheck","prompt":"Check again","in_secs":3600,"run_config":"Your saved profile"}}. The host clock resolves in_secs, exclusive with cron/once_local. run_config must name the actual caller profile: its agent-type default is never substituted. Create/update/re-enable validate saved profile names; unresolved names return valid-profile repair choices. list marks unresolved saved profiles with run_config_error and no next_run_ms. Failed agent-created runs notify the creator inbox once, including pre-spawn failures. Bound agents may omit id, repository, workspace, cron, enabled, grace_secs, overlap and max_duration_secs; unbound HTTP/IPC callers must supply all normal definition fields (cron may be omitted for Once). Missing context names the required field. Repeating an identical generated create for the same caller returns the first saved occurrence; use an explicit new id for a separate identical reminder. Create returns the saved definition with local fire time and next_run_ms; no date/list/get needed. update accepts definition or id+enabled; list/get/pause/resume/delete manage definitions (history retained). run_now/run/list_runs/summary manage runs; preview/preview_definition/preset resolve schedules; templates/template supply disabled drafts; worktree_preview/cleanup_worktree inspect/remove safe run workspaces.
telegram: Call register to opt your own MCP-bound TUIC agent into Telegram; it replaces the previous agent and sends it one TUIC notice. unregister releases your registration. Registration ends on agent exit, PTY close, MCP session end or daemon restart. Request-specific begin/activity/finish stay bound to the peer that received the request, even if another AI Chat connects. Explicit registration takeover revokes pending requests. Any live MCP-bound agent may send without registration or changing inbound ownership. Non-owner sends carry a server-derived [session name] prefix on every chunk, allow no buttons, and require a 30-second per-peer interval (telegram_sender_rate_limited). Owner sends have no prefix and preserve the authored text exactly. Reply to a prefixed message routes to the unique live peer with that exact name; absent, dead or ambiguous names fall back to the inbound owner. Names must be non-empty, at most 128 UTF-16 units, without brackets or control characters. With no registered agent, allowed inbound text goes to the latest-connected live AI Chat agent. Only when neither exists is text dropped after the bot replies No agent is listening. Ask an agent in TUICommander to register for Telegram.. TUIC acknowledges Telegram mail and opens its status draft automatically. begin is optional and idempotent for the current request, for PTY agents and AI Chat without a PTY. activity sends concise safe unapproved preview text. finish is authoritative: it sends the complete exact reply even after the draft or turn ended, and deduplicates completed requests. AI Chat streams only assistant message text; a Telegram-mail-woken turn settles to its own final text unless finish already replied. send uses the single allowlisted outbound destination with optional rows of {label,data} opaque buttons. Buttons return structured peer mail and confer no publish approval. No raw terminal output or hidden reasoning is streamed.
